# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for the reporting, coordination, and review of operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures that all incidents are managed in a timely and effective manner to minimize risk to personnel, passengers, and airport operations. The scope of this policy includes all incidents occurring on airside, landside, or within airport facilities that may impact safety, security, or operational efficiency. This policy applies to all staff, contractors, and third-party vendors operating within the airport environment.

## 2. Incident Categories

Operational incidents are categorized into four types: baggage, restricted-item, ramp safety, and equipment. Baggage incidents include any event involving lost, damaged, or misplaced luggage. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery of prohibited items, such as weapons or contraband, within airport premises. Ramp safety incidents encompass any event that compromises the safety of aircraft or personnel on the ramp area. Equipment incidents involve malfunctions or failures of airport equipment, including ground support equipment, baggage handling systems, or communication devices. Each category has specific reporting and response requirements, as outlined in the relevant policies.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All operational incidents must be reported immediately by the staff member who first identifies the incident. The reporting staff member is responsible for providing a clear and accurate description of the incident, including the location, time, and any immediate impact. The staff member must also initiate the first response, such as securing the area, ensuring the safety of personnel, and taking any necessary actions to mitigate the incident. For baggage incidents, the reporting staff member must ensure that the incident is escalated in accordance with AP-BAG-001 section 4. For restricted-item incidents, the reporting staff member must refer to AP-SEC-003 for guidance on handling and reporting procedures. All incidents must be documented in the airport's incident reporting system as soon as possible.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for managing the response to operational incidents and ensuring that all necessary actions are taken to address the incident. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record must include a detailed description of the incident, the actions taken, and any relevant information from the reporting staff member. The Incident Coordinator is also responsible for coordinating with the appropriate departments and personnel to ensure a timely and effective response. This includes liaising with the Airside Duty Manager and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that all aspects of the incident are addressed.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an incident, a post-incident review meeting must be conducted to assess the incident and identify any corrective actions required. The meeting must be chaired by the Incident Coordinator and attended by all relevant personnel, including the Airside Duty Manager and any affected departments. The review must include a detailed analysis of the incident, the root cause, and the effectiveness of the response. The meeting must also identify any corrective actions, improvements, or changes to procedures that may be necessary to prevent similar incidents in the future. All findings and actions from the review must be documented and shared with all relevant parties.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in the airport's incident reporting system and retained for a minimum of five years. Each record must include the incident description, the date and time of the incident, the location, the reporting staff member, the actions taken, and the outcome. The Incident Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all records are accurate, complete, and accessible to authorized personnel. Records must be reviewed periodically to ensure their integrity and to support continuous improvement in incident management.
